Title: Saifuddin warns of synthetic drugs that make users appear like 'zombies'
Article:
MACHANG: The emergence of synthetic drugs that can drastically alter users' behaviour, making them appear like "zombies", is a growing concern, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said there had been cases of people killing their spouses, parents and friends, with drug use showing a clear correlation with such violent incidents.
"If we look at these cases, they are closely linked to drug consumption," he told reporters.
Saifuddin said drug use patterns varied by region, with synthetic drugs more prevalent on the east coast, while drug abuse on the west coast involved a mixture of substances.
However, he said synthetic drug use remained high nationwide, partly because the substances were more easily accessible.
He said the National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) had three main functions: education and prevention, enforcement, and rehabilitation at its treatment centres.
On the 224 hotspots for undocumented migrants identified nationwide by the Immigration Department, Saifuddin said the locations had been mapped using data gathered through ongoing enforcement raids.
The data enabled the department to identify areas where foreigners frequently lived, stayed or gathered.
He said enforcement operations at these locations generally uncovered four categories of foreigners.
They comprised those who entered the country without travel or immigration documents, those whose passes had expired, those with valid passes, including work or student passes, who had misused them, and those classified as refugees.

Title: Residents complain of recurring floods in Petaling Jaya, Subang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy rain has prompted complaints from residents about recurring floods in parts of the Klang Valley, with one resident blaming clogged drains near an unfinished pedestrian walkway in Petaling Jaya.
In a post on Threads, user _anuarlatif said flooding frequently occurred in Taman Putra Damai, Lembah Subang, which the user attributed to blocked drains following construction work along the area's main road.
The user said soil and construction materials left by the roadside appeared to have washed into the drains, obstructing water flow.
"Can the minister look into the problems residents here face whenever it rains, causing floods in our neighbourhood?
"The pedestrian walkway has been left unfinished for a long time. The problem stems from the contractor building the walkway along the main road.
[[nid:1557607]]
"When it rains, soil and materials fall into the drains, eventually blocking the water flow," the user said in a post today.
The Petaling Jaya City Council said the user should provide the full address of the affected area to facilitate checks and further action.
Meanwhile, another Threads user, amm.yusopp, reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.
Further details on the flooding at both locations, including water levels and the impact on residents, were not available.

Title: Saifuddin hands new identity card to 70-year-old Kelantan woman
Article:
MACHANG: After years of carrying a damaged identity card that was barely legible, 70-year-old Minah Yacob was relieved to receive her new-generation MyKad.
The Pangkal Payong resident received the card from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail during the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Handing Minah the card, Saifuddin said: "Congratulations. Here is your new identity card."
Minah said her old identity card had been damaged for several years and was almost falling apart, making the information on it difficult to read.
The mother of six, who earns a living making and selling kuih, said receiving the new card had brought her considerable relief.
"I am very happy and relieved to finally have a new MyKad.
"My old identity card had been badly damaged for years, and the information on it could hardly be read," she said.
The New Generation MyKad is a version of the national identity card introduced by the National Registration Department, with improvements to its design, security features and functions.
It was issued in phases beginning Sept 17

Title: 1.2 million workers yet to join Lindung 24 Jam scheme
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Some 1.2 million workers who had previously opted not to contribute to the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam scheme have been urged to take up the protection following the announcement of an additional annual tax relief of RM150 under the 2027 Budget.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the incentive offered workers a good opportunity to resume contributions to ensure they had social security protection in the event of accidents outside working hours.
He said the importance of such protection was underscored by the 10,424 claims recorded under the scheme from June 1 to Sept 30, equivalent to an average of 85 cases a day.
"These figures remind us that accidents can happen at any time and that financial protection is crucial when someone faces adversity," he told reporters after launching the i Lindung u Gegar @ Melaka programme at Dataran Keris today.
He said the government understood public concerns over disposable income amid inflationary pressures driven by global factors, but social security protection must remain a priority.
Ramanan said the proposed Traveller Scheme for 480,000 Malaysians who travel daily to Singapore would be tabled in Parliament during the current sitting and implemented as promised by the prime minister when he announced it on Labour Day.
He also urged gig economy platform providers to utilise the RM30 million 2027 Budget allocation under the Lindung Kendiri scheme by co-funding contributions, which would boost the matching social security rate from 35 percent to 50 percent for gig workers earning RM3,000 or less.
"We also want to remind platform providers that enforcement to ensure compliance with Perkeso contributions began on Oct 1, including the obligation to make mandatory contribution deductions and integrate their respective systems with Perkeso's system," he said.
Meanwhile, the first i Lindung u Gegar @ Melaka programme held in the state targets 15,000 visitors as part of efforts by the Human Resources Ministry and Perkeso to bring government services closer to the public.
At the same programme, 400 housewives in Melaka were registered as Lindung Kasih contributors, making them eligible for Perkeso protection in the event of unforeseen mishaps.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt allocates RM3.1b under 2027 Budget for Islamic development
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Madani government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under the 2027 Budget to strengthen Islamic development, including the empowerment of religious educational institutions and safeguarding the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government's commitment to implementing a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.
"The Madani government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for
sekolah agama rakyat
(community religious schools),
tahfiz
institutions and
sekolah pondok
(traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
"The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions," he said in a statement today.
Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including
Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain
(KAFA) teachers,
takmir
teachers, imams, bilals,
tok siaks
,
nojas
and
marbuts
, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 KAFA teachers who teach students with special needs, including those who use sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.
"The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 imam, bilal,
tok siak
, mosque staff and
takmir
teachers.
"The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the
ummah
," he said.
In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of
diyat
, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person's actions.
He said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.
In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300
pondok
schools nationwide.
Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government's approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.
"This Budget framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground. We aim to elevate the nation's economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision," he said.
He added that the government's priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians.
TAGS: Zulkifli Hasan, Budget 2027, Islamic teachings, education, welfare

Title: MAIS denies claims that Nik Nazmi's khalwat case was a "frame-up"
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) has denied allegations that the action against former Setiawangsa member of parliament Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) over a khalwat (proximity) case was an act of persecution or a "frame-up".
MAIS chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said JAIS acted based on an official complaint and in accordance with established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual.
"The suggestion that the religious department was involved in manipulation or anything of the sort is entirely untrue. We have a legal obligation...when a complaint is lodged, we are required to conduct a thorough investigation.
"Rest assured, JAIS will carry out the investigation as diligently as possible, and if there is clear evidence, we will proceed with charges in court," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the 2026 Gathering of Accredited Religious Teachers in Selangor at the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Silver Jubilee Hall here. Also present was Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.
Salehuddin said the case was made public to clarify that Syariah laws were enforced fairly, regardless of the background or influence of the individual under investigation.
He called on the public to allow JAIS sufficient time and space to complete its investigation and refrain from speculation that could compromise the fairness of the legal process.
"We cannot pass judgment while the investigation is still incomplete. We must act fairly and carry out our duties in accordance with the regulations. If we were to act outside these regulations, we ourselves would be subject to accusations," he said.
Nik Nazmi, on Instagram, had confirmed that
he was one of two people detained
by JAIS in Petaling Jaya last Thursday over allegations of khalwat. He said he was prepared to cooperate with any legal proceedings.
Earlier today, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari
dismissed claims
that it was weaponising khalwat claims against rival political leaders to weaken opponents.
"We have better things to do than set up khalwat traps," he was quoted as saying.
Nik Nazmi and Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli had
left PKR,
vacating their Setiawangsa and Pandan parliamentary seats to set up the independent party Bersama.
Meanwhile, on a separate case involving a local youth suspected of participating in the rituals of another religion, Salehuddin said preliminary findings suggested that the individual's actions were, so far, a matter of personal belief.
However, he said JAIS was examining various forms of digital evidence, including social media posts concerning rituals at Batu Caves that had been linked to other belief systems.
"The public must understand that when we intend to take legal action in court, we must ensure that all evidence is authentic. We are aware that material could potentially be superimposed or generated via AI (artificial intelligence); therefore, we have experts who can verify its authenticity.
"Regarding the issue of apostasy, we cannot impose penalties without conducting a thorough investigation. We certainly consult with the relevant authorities before taking action against anyone.
"A comprehensive investigation must be carried out first," he said.
On Oct 13, JAIS director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said a man who went viral over allegations that he had performed rituals of another religion, which is in breach of Syariah law, had been detained alongside his mother in Kuala Lumpur to assist in an investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police seize 125 motorcycles in Op Samseng Jalanan in Kuala Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Police issued 447 summonses and seized 125 motorcycles during 'Op Samseng Jalanan 2026', a two-day operation conducted at two locations in Kuala Terengganu.
District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the action followed inspections on motorcycles believed to have been involved in the Gen-Y Event 2026 celebrations.
He said the offences detected included missing side mirrors, failure to display a valid motor vehicle licence, expired motor vehicle licences, non-compliant number plates and modified motorcycle exhausts.
"The operation was conducted on Oct 16 and 17 following public complaints about a group of youths riding motorcycles dangerously and causing noise in the Kampung Padang Midin residential area and Kuala Terengganu city centre.
"A total of 125 motorcycles were seized for various offences under Section 64 of the Road Transport Act 1987. The operation was carried out from midnight until the early hours of the morning," he said in a statement today.
Police advised the public to comply with traffic laws and refrain from dangerous riding, which poses a risk to themselves and other road users.

Title: Missing father, son found safe in Besut forest after 3 days
Article:
JERTIH: A man and his son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today.
The two men, Adam Adnan, 25, and his father Adnan Mohamad, 57, were found by a search and rescue (SAR) team at 12.40pm, about 3km from the operation's command post.
Besut police chief superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said they were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area.
"The two men were found weak after going without food for three days while lost in the forest.
"They were assisted down by the rescue team before being taken by a Civil Defence Force (CDF) ambulance to Besut Hospital for treatment," he told reporters today.
It was reported earlier today that the
father and son
had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PHEB gives aid to families affected by Nepal-Tibet tragedy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) has given one-off financial aid to families affected by the Aug 26 Nepal-Tibet border tragedy.
PHEB deputy chairman Senator Dr Lingeshwaran R. Arunasalam said four families from Penang were identified, with three accepting the RM5,000 assistance.
Speaking at the aid handover ceremony, Lingeshwaran urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the federal government to consider similar one-off assistance for all affected Malaysian families nationwide.
Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, who attended the event, extended her condolences to the families and commended PHEB's welfare efforts.
She said her ministry, through the National Welfare Foundation, was providing RM500 to each affected family, while her office was contributing an additional RM1,000 per family. Emotional distress and psychosocial support were also available through the Talian Kasih helpline at 15999.
Bukit Gelugor MP Ramkarpal Singh contributed RM5,000 to one affected family from his constituency.
PHEB chairman RSN Rayer urged authorities to expedite the
legal declaration of death,
issuance of death certificates and other official documentation to help families settle insurance claims, property transfers and urgent financial matters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Disabled person rescued from flood-hit home in Seberang Prai
Article:
SEBERANG PRAI: A person with disabilities was rescued after being trapped inside a flood-hit home in Mengkuang Titi.
The incident occurred after flash floods inundated several areas in the Seberang Prai Tengah district at about 4pm.
Members of the Seberang Prai Tengah Civil Defence Force (CDF) rescued the victim from the rising floodwaters.
Further details on other affected areas and the total number of evacuees will be updated as official reports from local authorities become available.

Title: Myanmar man held with 10 others attempting to leave country illegally
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Myanmar man believed to be acting as a transporter was arrested with 10 fellow citizens during an Immigration Department raid at a hotel in Wakaf Che Yeh.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the group comprised six men and four women who were believed to be working in Johor Baru and Kuala Lumpur.
He said they arrived in Kelantan at about 6.30am and checked into the hotel, which was believed to be a temporary transit point.
At 8.30am, the Kelantan Immigration Department raided the hotel and foiled an attempt to take all 10 undocumented migrants out of the country through an illegal route for their return to Myanmar.
Officers also found a Honda CR-V sport utility vehicle believed to have been used to transport the migrants, along with several bags belonging to them.
Preliminary investigations found that each Myanmar citizen was required to pay the transporter RM3,500 to be taken out of the country.
Lokman Effendi said the transporter, who was in his 30s, admitted to having lived in Shah Alam, Selangor, for four years.
All 11 were detained to assist investigations under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
In a separate operation at a construction site in Kubang Kerian, the Kelantan Immigration Department inspected 57 foreign workers and detained 55 on suspicion of various immigration offences, Lokman Effendi said.
From Jan 1 to Oct 15, the department conducted 11,000 enforcement operations nationwide, during which more than 146,000 foreign workers were inspected.
More than 65,000 people were detained for various immigration offences, while more than 45,000 foreign workers were repatriated to their countries of origin.
Lokman Effendisaid the 11,000 operations carried out over 287 days amounted to an average of about 38 operations a day.
On average, about 511 foreign workers were inspected daily, while 228 people were detained for various immigration offences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sri Lanka suffers nationwide electricity blackout
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka suffered a nationwide electricity blackout on Saturday after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption, officials said.
The country was without grid power for more than two hours, with no clear timeline for when electricity would be restored.
State-run Electricity Distribution Lanka (EDL) said engineers were working to fix a fault affecting the entire grid and suspected excess solar power had caused the breakdown.
Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka said authorities hoped to restore supplies "stage by stage".
"We request rooftop solar system owners to disconnect their systems until further instructions in order to support the restoration efforts," he said in a brief statement.
The entire grid shut down in February 2025, when solar power generation exceeded consumption on a bright, sunny Sunday. It took more than six hours to restore supplies.
Sri Lanka has an installed solar power capacity of just over 3,000 megawatts, while daytime demand ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 megawatts.
Tax concessions have encouraged consumers to switch to solar power and sell their surplus electricity to the grid, creating imbalances that the utility provider is struggling to manage.
The government aims to increase solar power generation capacity to nearly 4,400 megawatts within three years — a 388 per cent increase from 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 25 monitoring stations record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 25 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest at 198.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System, Negri Sembilan's Nilai and Seremban recorded readings of 180 and 176 respectively.
In Johor, Larkin recorded an API reading of 175, followed by Pengerang (174), Kota Tinggi (173), Batu Pahat (171), Tangkak (167), Segamat (161) and Kluang (161).
In Selangor, Shah Alam and Johan Setia recorded readings of 172 each, followed by Klang (171), Petaling Jaya (169), Banting (160) and Kuala Selangor (109).
In Melaka, Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai recorded readings of 168 each, while Bandaraya Melaka recorded 162.
Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 166, while Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 164 and 163 respectively.
In Sabah, Sandakan recorded a reading of 157, while Tawau recorded 129.
Another 42 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality.
These included Seri Manjung in Perak, with an API reading of 96, followed by Tanjung Malim (91), Pegoh in Ipoh (89) and Tasek in Ipoh (88).
In Sarawak, the Serian police headquarters monitoring station recorded a reading of 82, followed by Sri Aman (80) and Samarahan (79).
In Pahang, Rompin recorded an API reading of 78, followed by Temerloh (76) and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (75).
Limbang in Sarawak was the only monitoring station to record good air quality, with an API reading of 50.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas has list of candidates ready for Melaka polls, says Hadi
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Pas has prepared a list of potential candidates for the upcoming Melaka election, with the final selection to be decided by the party's central leadership.
Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the list contained numerous names for consideration.
"There are many candidates on the list. Deciding who will ultimately contest is up to the Pas central leadership," he told a press conference after launching the Tafsir Al-Tibyan book here today.
He was responding to questions about Pas' candidates after Barisan Nasional confirmed that its candidate list was complete.
Yesterday, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the coalition's list was ready and could be announced at any time.
Rauf was reported to have said he would not take long to announce the candidates as nomination day was approaching.
On the number of seats Pas would contest in the Melaka election, Hadi, who is also the Marang member of parliament, said discussions were still ongoing.
"The number of seats is still under discussion. The matter is still being discussed.
"It will be announced closer to nomination day," he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
Melaka has 28 state seats. BN won 21 in the previous election, while Pakatan Harapan won five and Perikatan Nasional secured two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorists call for action over daily gridlock along Jalan Maarof
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists plying Jalan Maarof in Bangsar are calling on authorities to address severe daily traffic gridlocks affecting commutes into the commercial hub.
Drivers said the stretch turns into a persistent bottleneck during peak hours, driven by heavy traffic merging from multiple directions into narrow two-lane roads.
Personal driver Muhammad Naim, 35, said the area experiences congestion during morning, noon, and evening rush hours.
"Traffic comes in from three different directions, including Pantai and Brickfields, alongside cars making U-turns. Everything squeezes into just two narrow lanes, so a bottleneck is bound to happen," he told the New Straits Times.
Naim added that indiscriminate roadside parking exacerbates the congestion.
"The road is just too narrow for so many cars. It only has two lanes handling heavy traffic, and when cars are parked along the roadside, it makes it even harder to move through.
"This has been going on for years. It's a main road leading to Bangsar Shopping Centre and Damansara, making it one of the worst traffic spots around here," he said, proposing that traffic wardens be stationed to direct merging traffic.
Grab driver Zarif Fadli, 25, said peak-hour congestion extends from Jalan Bangsar all the way up to Jalan Maarof.
"Whether it is the morning rush, the evening commute, or the stretch heading towards Mid Valley, drivers are constantly stuck in traffic.
"The jam from Jalan Bangsar is bad in the morning and evening, especially during peak hours. Double parking along the road makes it much worse. We need better public transport services so people don't have to drive into Bangsar every day," he said.
Food delivery rider Pankaj Kumar, 56, a 25-year resident, said gridlock across Bangsar and neighbouring Brickfields has turned daily travel into a hassle.
"Driving around Bangsar and Brickfields is absolute torture. The gridlock is unavoidable during morning and evening rush hours, but it now happens even on weekends and rainy days.
"The issue is indiscriminate parking and rampant double parking. People park illegally and claim it is 'just for five minutes', but then leave their cars for half an hour or two hours," he said, urging Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to step up patrols and enforcement.
Bukit Bandaraya Residents Association adviser Datuk M. Ali said traffic enforcement in the city has largely collapsed, leading to widespread double parking and severe bottlenecks.
"Strict, consistent, and persistent enforcement without compromise is urgently needed to tackle the worsening traffic congestion. People must be made to be disciplined and accountable. If they are not adhering to persuasion, then go in and use a hard stick instead of a carrot," he said.
Ali noted that while authorities occasionally issue summonses following public complaints, DBKL should leverage surveillance cameras across the capital to monitor traffic and conduct random towing of illegally parked vehicles.
The New Straits Times has reached out to DBKL for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MOH officers killed in helicopter crash receive posthumous promotions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Four Health Ministry (MOH) officers who died in a helicopter crash while on duty on Sept 8 have been promoted posthumously in recognition of their service and dedication.
The ministry honoured the healthcare staff who served with the
Flying Doctor Service
(PDU), whose promotions were approved by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on Oct 13.
The board cleared 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the ministry for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15, the ministry said in a statement.
The approvals reflect the ministry's continued efforts to recognise officers' commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.
In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under the ministry's teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.
The approval provides the officers concerned with better opportunities for career advancement.
The ministry expressed confidence that such recognition would encourage continued excellence and strengthen officers' commitment to building a high-quality, sustainable and responsive national healthcare system.
It said it would continue to review and implement improvements to ensure officers' welfare and career development received due attention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan retracts mistaken magnitude 9.9 quake alert
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's weather agency withdrew an erroneous alert for a magnitude 9.9 earthquake minutes after issuing it, apologising for a warning that disrupted transport.
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) had initially warned on Friday that a magnitude 9.9 earthquake had occurred near the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Chishima Islands, triggering loud emergency alerts on millions of mobile phones.
The JMA later clarified that a magnitude 6.9 quake had occurred near Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula at a depth of 160km just after midday.
"We deeply apologise for the significant inconvenience and concern caused to the public," JMA official Shinya Tsukada told reporters.
The alert did not cause widespread panic but briefly disrupted public transport.
According to the JMA, the error stemmed from an anomaly in calculating the earthquake's epicentre.
The estimated magnitude was based on an incorrect assumption that the epicentre was about 680 kilometres farther from Japan than it actually was, the weather agency said.
Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive magnitude 9.0 undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.
A magnitude 9.9 tremor would have released about 22 times as much energy as the 2011 quake, according to local media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four states exceed national drug involvement threshold
Article:
MACHANG: Four states — Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu — have recorded drug involvement rates above the national threshold, with Pendang in Kedah and Kuala Krai in Kelantan emerging as the country's two highest-ranking districts.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures were calculated based on the number of people involved in drug cases per 100,000 population, using an international standard adopted by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
He said Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, were also identified as critical districts, with rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.
"These are all concerns for us, and not just for one state.
"Besides Kelantan, three other states are also showing worrying figures and an increasing trend," he told reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Saifuddin said drug abuse among children below 15 was also becoming increasingly worrying, while those aged between 15 and 39 remained the largest group involved in drug abuse based on available profiles.
He said the trend called for more comprehensive preventive measures, including early education and greater parental involvement, to prevent young people from becoming involved in drug abuse.
"The National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) has three main functions — education and prevention, enforcement, and rehabilitation.
"We must strengthen public education to raise awareness and encourage families to take preventive action," he said.
On efforts to curb drug-related activities along the Kelantan-Thailand border, Saifuddin said he had directed the Kelantan police chief to ensure round-the-clock surveillance along all stretches of the border.
He said the strategy included maintaining a visible police presence, demolishing illegal jetties and enforcing the Immigration Act against undocumented cross-border movements.
However, he acknowledged that these measures could not completely eliminate the problem, as drug-related crime was linked to organised criminal networks that had been operating for decades.
"Our actions can help reduce the problem, but they cannot eliminate it entirely.
"This is the responsibility of the Home Ministry and the police, but it is not enough. It must be a shared responsibility," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 75pct of prison inmates serving sentences for drug offences, says Saifuddin
Article:
MACHANG: About 75 per cent of inmates in prisons nationwide are serving sentences for drug-related offences, with the proportion exceeding 90 per cent at Machang Prison, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said Malaysia had 41 prisons housing between 90,000 and 100,000 inmates, with drug-related offences accounting for the bulk of cases.
"Among the offences are those under Sections 15(1), 12(2) and 39 of the Dangerous Drugs Act," he told reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Saifuddin said Pengkalan Chepa Prison was the most overcrowded prison in the country
He said profiling of drug offenders showed that those aged between 15 and 39 remained the largest group involved in drug abuse, while the growing trend among children below 15 was also a cause for concern.
He said the trend required more comprehensive preventive measures, including early education and greater parental involvement to keep young people away from drugs.
"The National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) has three main functions — education and prevention, enforcement, and rehabilitation — to address drug abuse.
"Public education efforts must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage families to take preventive action," he said.
On the Kampung Angkat Madani programme, Saifuddin said several projects had been implemented at Kampung Gosong to improve facilities and residents' well-being.
Upgrading works had been carried out at Surau Kampung Gosong and Masjid Bilal, including improvements to prayer areas, toilets, bathrooms, ablution facilities, public address systems and other interior amenities.
"Lighting has also been installed at the village cemetery after residents informed us that burials sometimes had to be carried out at night," he said.
He said 14 houses had also been upgraded through cooperation with Akademi Binaan Malaysia, involving 10 individuals supervised by the Prisons Department and Rela members.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry's 11 agencies were allowed to select a school and a village each year under the programmes.
The initiative had been implemented for three consecutive years, covering 33 villages and 33 schools nationwide.
"This is something we are proud of at the Home Ministry. From the north to the south, including Sabah and Sarawak, we have reached villages selected based on their potential to bring significant added value to local communities," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected across country until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to affect parts of the country until 6pm.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a warning issued at 3.15pm, said adverse weather conditions were forecast to affect the whole of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Perak, Selangor, Melaka and Johor, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
The same conditions were expected in several areas of Terengganu (Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Kemaman, Besut and Setiu); Kelantan (Gua Musang, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Pasir Mas); Pahang (Bentong, Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, Kuantan, Pekan, Rompin and Maran); and Negeri Sembilan (Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin).
In Sarawak, the affected areas were Kuching, Samarahan, Serian (Serian and Siburan), Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu (Tatau), Kapit (Song), Miri and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning covered Tawau, Kunak, Lahad Datu, the West Coast (Kota Belud, Putatan, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Papar), the Interior (Beaufort, Sipitang, Tambunan and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu) and Sandakan (Kinabatangan).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates - Amirudin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR will field a mix of seasoned and experienced candidates, young people and women from various ethnic groups in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the party's candidates will be individuals capable of serving the community and possessing qualities that can help secure victory in the state constituencies they contest.
"In some state constituencies where our support is relatively low, we will allow candidates to gain experience. This is part of the party's and Pakatan Harapan's (PH) long-term plan," he told reporters after attending the Semarak Kasih event with Yayasan Selangor students today.
Asked about cooperation with other parties, Amirudin, who is also PKR election director, said a decision will be made within the next one to two weeks.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said yesterday that the party would contest nine seats in the Melaka state election, with its list of candidates to be announced by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, on Oct 24.
The Election Commission has set
Nov 14
as polling day for the Melaka state polls, with early voting on Nov 10 and nomination day on Oct 31.
Melaka has 28 state assembly seats, with Barisan Nasional (BN) winning 21 in the previous state election, PH securing five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) taking the remaining two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi for 3 months over khalwat case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has suspended its co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months.
The decision follows his admission that he was detained by religious authorities on suspicion of khalwat (close proximity) in Petaling Jaya on Oct 15.
The suspension takes effect from Oct 20 until Jan 19, 2027.
Bersama president Syukri Razab said the party took note of Nik Nazmi's admission and viewed the matter seriously.
He said issues involving party leaders and members must be addressed appropriately to safeguard the party's integrity, credibility and public confidence.
"Bersama takes this development seriously and maintains that every issue involving the party's leadership and members must be handled appropriately to preserve the party's integrity, credibility and public trust," he said in a statement today.
Syukri said the suspension was necessary and reasonable.
However, he stressed that the decision did not diminish Nik Nazmi's contributions and commitment to the party since its relaunch in May this year.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1557338/nik-nazmi-admits-being-detained-khalwat-apologises-wife-bersama-watch#google_vignette
Nik Nazmi, a former natural resources and environmental sustainability minister, earlier admitted that he was one of two people detained by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) on suspicion of khalwat in Petaling Jaya on Oct 15.
He said he was with a woman when Jais officers arrived but denied that they had committed any indecent acts.
"I admit that it was a mistake. As I also informed the Jais officer, we indeed did not commit any indecent acts that would raise suspicion," he said in an earlier statement.
Nik Nazmi said he and his friends had initially held a discussion at a studio in Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur, before continuing it in Petaling Jaya to review materials related to a project.
He said only he and the woman were present when Jais officers arrived.
He apologised to his wife, family, Bersama members and supporters over the incident, acknowledging that his lapse in judgement had affected the party.
He also pledged to cooperate fully with any legal proceedings and said he would accept any decision made by the party leadership.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad had confirmed the detention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Army to review SOP after personnel arrested with pistol, ammunition
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The army will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur.
Army chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army's continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified.
"The same applies to this case. We are constantly monitoring. Although an SOP is already in place, we are always looking at continuous improvement," he told reporters after the Passing Out Parade of Young Male Soldiers Series 206/26, involving 1,485 soldiers.
The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Azhan said the personnel, who is in his 30s, was undergoing a six-month transition training programme and was scheduled to complete his service in three months.
"The individual is undergoing transition training before completing his service and is currently detained at Sungai Buloh Prison for the trial process and further action," he said.
Meanwhile, Malek Razak said the armed forces had its own procedures and investigation protocols for handling cases involving its personnel to ensure that all actions were taken in accordance with established regulations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police to complete probe involving MCBA chief after A-GC seeks improvements
Article:
MACHANG: Police are completing their investigation into an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 after the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) returned the investigation papers.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the A-GC requested several improvements to the investigation papers before deciding on the next course of action.
He said although the papers were initially submitted to the A-GC within a week, prosecution authorities required further clarification and additional investigative work.
"The police are still completing the investigation. The A-GC has stated that several improvements need to be made to the investigation papers.
"The investigation papers contain statements recorded from witnesses and all information gathered during the investigation before being submitted to the A-GC.
"The A-GC must be fully satisfied with the findings before making a decision. Usually, if it is not satisfied, it will return the investigation papers to the police for further action," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Saifuddin added that police have been instructed to complete the investigation in accordance with the A-GC's requirements.
The A-GC returned the
investigation paper
to the police on Oct 8.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar previously confirmed the paper was returned to enable further investigation into the incident involving the MCBA director-general.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six agencies swoop on Gombak premises, six Pakistanis detained
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six Pakistanis were detained for suspected immigration offences during a multi-agency enforcement operation at two religious premises in Gombak, Selangor, yesterday.
The operation involved 207 personnel from six enforcement agencies, with 184 people inspected at the two locations in Batu Caves.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the operation was coordinated by the Gombak district police headquarters and involved the police, Home Ministry, Immigration Department, Selayang Municipal Council, fire and rescue department and Registrar of Societies (ROS).
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 76 people were brought to the Gombak district police headquarters for further checks following enforcement activities at a mosque in Kampung Nakhoda and another religious premises along Jalan Laksamana in Kampung Laksamana.
He said the six Pakistanis were detained after checks on their documents revealed suspected offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, which concerns foreigners entering or remaining in Malaysia without valid passes or permits.
Shazeli said the Home Ministry also took enforcement action over offences under the Printing Presses and Publications Act 1984 and the Printing of Quranic Texts Act 1986.
Meanwhile, ROS seized documents and other materials for further examination.
The Selayang Municipal Council also took action over business licensing violations and unauthorised construction activities, including issuing notices and carrying out seizures under the relevant laws.
Inspections by the Fire and Rescue Department found fire safety non-compliance, including insufficient fire extinguishers and inadequate emergency exits in buildings.
Shazeli said the respective agencies would take further action within their jurisdictions.
He also clarified that the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) was not involved in the operation.
The operation was conducted smoothly without any untoward incidents, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak election could be held as early as December
Article:
KUCHING: The 13th Sarawak election could be held as early as December this year.
Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the dissolution of the state legislative assembly would ultimately depend on the decision of Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg.
Karim said the current term of the Sarawak assembly would automatically expire in February 2027 after completing its five-year term.
"Once the assembly is dissolved, the Election Commission (EC) is required under electoral law to hold an election within 60 days.
"Some say it could be held as late as February, but I see December as the likely period, based on the assembly's five-year term," he told reporters today.
He said if the assembly were dissolved in late October or November, the EC would need time to meet and determine the election dates, as well as set a campaign period that typically lasts about two weeks.
Karim said holding the election in January or February would be less suitable because of several festive celebrations and Ramadan, leaving a narrower window for the polls.
"So, we only have November and the first half of December. It may happen, or it may not. Everything depends on when the assembly is dissolved.
"I can say that the dissolution will take place soon," he said.
Karim, who is the information chief of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), said Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) was ready for the state election, adding that opposition parties were also expected to be making preparations.
He said the decision on GPS candidates would be left to the coalition's top leadership, although he expected changes to the line-up at every election to ensure leadership continuity.
"At every election, at least 10 per cent of candidates may be replaced, and among the 10 to 30 per cent of new candidates, we must also take into account the roles of women and young people," he said.
On GPS's chances of retaining its two-thirds majority, he said the coalition was confident of maintaining its performance but would not take any of Sarawak's 82 state seats for granted.
"Every seat is important. We cannot assume there are white, grey or black seats because we must respect voters and ensure they have the best elected representatives," he said.
Asked about the future of the Asajaya seat, which he has held for about 25 years, Karim said he would leave the decision to the Sarawak Premier.
He said he was also prepared to step aside if the leadership felt it was time to give younger candidates an opportunity.
"I am ready to make way and support whoever is chosen. But I leave that decision to the Premier," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says Google rejected his idea to rename ocean after him
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday told supporters about his alleged attempt to have an ocean named after him and Google's refusal to go along with the idea, reported German news agency dpa.
Speaking at a campaign rally in Georgia, Trump claimed he had suggested to representatives of the internet giant that either the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean be renamed the "Trump Ocean". According to Trump, they responded indignantly: "We've had it. That's enough. We're not doing any more."
Trump had already renamed the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" by executive order in 2025, followed by Lake Ontario on the Canadian border, which he renamed "Lake America" in August this year. Google Maps adopted both changes for users in the United States.
Trump told supporters he had sent Google a map labelled "Trump Ocean", but company representatives rejected the idea.
"Sir, look, okay, this one we can't do. Oceans are different. Oceans cover many, many countries. We can't do it," Trump quoted them as saying.
Trump said he had only been joking — this time — but added that it was not the worst idea he had ever had.
It was not immediately clear whether the exchange with Google had actually taken place.
Trump has repeatedly suggested that he would like to rename an ocean. He has also floated the idea of renaming the Strait of Hormuz the "Trump Strait", apparently in an attempt to provoke Iran, with which the US is at war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia eyes bigger role in global maritime dispute resolution - Chief Justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's strategic location between the Straits of Melaka, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, and the South China Sea strengthens its role in resolving international commercial and maritime disputes, said Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.
He said Malaysia has long had a specialised Admiralty Court, and the establishment of the International Commercial and Admiralty Division (ICAD) has brought admiralty and international commercial cases under a single specialised division.
Established at the High Court here on March 2 this year, ICAD is expected to boost investor confidence in Kuala Lumpur as a regional hub for business and dispute resolution.
Wan Ahmad Farid said that delays of even a few days in urgent admiralty cases could have significant commercial consequences, particularly when disputes involved vessels, cargo and parties across several jurisdictions.
"Applications for the arrest or release of vessels, the provision of security and other urgent matters require prompt attention, and a delay of even a few days can have significant commercial consequences," he said in his keynote address at the inaugural ICAD Conference 2026 at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) today.
Wan Ahmad Farid said maritime disputes were inherently international, often involving vessels registered in one country, owned by companies in another, financed by banks in a third and carrying cargo belonging to parties across several jurisdictions.
"A vessel may be registered in one country, owned by a company in another, financed by a bank in a third, chartered by an entity in a fourth, and carrying cargo belonging to parties in several more.
"Admiralty disputes are inherently international, involving vessel arrests, charterparty disputes, cargo claims, maritime security and arbitration.
"The trade that passes through generates disputes over cargo, charterparties, finance, insurance, energy and infrastructure,'  he said.
He said geography alone is not enough as ICAD's role is to transform Malaysia's geographical advantage into a jurisdictional advantage by ensuring disputes could be resolved close to where the business is done, by judges who understand its commercial and maritime context.
He said a premier dispute resolution forum was built on trust, which could not be bought or established overnight but had to be earned over time.
"It is earned when foreign investors know that if they bring a dispute to Malaysia, they will receive justice that is blind to nationality, deeply sophisticated in commercial logic and fiercely independent.
"Roads and ports carry goods. Certainty and trust carry confidence, and confidence carries capital.
"Let us build this infrastructure deliberately, protect it carefully, and offer it to the world with integrity," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Local cocoa production needs boost to cut import reliance
Article:
MELAKA: Malaysia needs to boost local cocoa bean production to reduce reliance on imports, as the processing industry depends heavily on foreign supplies.
Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said stronger local production was needed to strengthen the cocoa supply chain and ensure growers benefited from the industry's expansion.
She said Malaysia's exports of cocoa beans and cocoa-based products rose from RM15.06 billion in 2024 to RM18.33 billion last year, highlighting the industry's growth potential.
However, growth in cocoa processing needed to be matched by higher local bean production so growers could also benefit, she said when opening A Malaysian Cocoa Affair 2026, organised by the Malaysian Cocoa Board (MCB) at a shopping centre in Banda Hilir today.
Also present were Plantation and Commodities Ministry secretary-general Datuk Yusran Shah Mohd Yusof and MCB director-general Shari Fuddin Sha'ari.
The ministry is focusing on increasing local production and smallholders' incomes through group planting, rehabilitating less productive farms and providing planting materials from high-quality cocoa clones.
"We do not want the industry to grow only at the processing level while local growers fail to receive their fair share of the benefits," Noraini said.
The ministry is also strengthening the National Cocoa Traceability System to identify the origin of cocoa beans and record their movement from farms to processing facilities.
Noraini said this was important to ensure
Malaysian cocoa products
met international market requirements, including the European Union Deforestation Regulation.
More than RM40 million was allocated under 2027 Budget to support the development of high-value cocoa products using modern technology, including premium chocolate made through the bean-to-bar method, she said.
Malaysia also aims to develop more local chocolate brands capable of entering international markets.
Noraini encouraged more young people to enter the cocoa industry, including in chocolate making, product design, marketing, research and entrepreneurship, to strengthen the sector's future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After another downpour, Lembah Subang resident asks minister to step in over recurring floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Flash floods hit several parts of the Klang Valley after heavy rain this afternoon, as a Lembah Subang resident raised concerns over recurring floods in the neighbourhood, alleging that an unfinished pedestrian walkway project may be obstructing nearby drains.
Flooding was reported in several areas, including USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with inundated roads disrupting traffic.
“Can the minister look into the problems faced by residents here, who have to deal with flooding in our neighbourhood every time it rains?” Threads user _anuarlatif said in a post today.
The user alleged that soil and construction materials left beside the main road in Taman Putra Damai, Lembah Subang, had entered nearby drains, blocking the flow of water during rain.
The user also claimed that work on the pedestrian walkway had remained unfinished for a long time, blaming the contractor for the recurring problem.
“When it rains, soil and materials fall into the drains, eventually blocking them,” the user said.
Threads user _anuarlatif highlighted the recurrent flooding in his Lembah Subang neighborhood after a heavy downpour on October 17, 2026, which he believes is caused by leftover construction material flowing into the drains and causing blockage. — Threads screenshots
Petaling Jaya City Council acknowledged the complaint and asked the user to provide the full address of the affected location so it could check the site and determine what further action was needed.
“Please provide the full address of the affected location to facilitate checks and further action by the council,” the council said.
Another Threads user, amm.yusopp, also reported flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang.
The alleged link between the unfinished walkway and the recurring floods has not been independently verified, while details on the extent of flooding at the two neighbourhoods and its impact on residents were not immediately available.

Title: Missing father and son found weak after three days in Terengganu forest without food
Article:
JERTIH, Oct 17 — A father and son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today.
Adam Adnan, 25, and his father Adnan Mohamad, 57, were found by a search and rescue (SAR) team at 12.40pm, about three kilometres from the operation’s command post.
Besut police chief Supt Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said the two were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area.
“The two men were found weak after going without food for three days while lost in the forest.
“They were assisted down by the rescue team before being taken by a Civil Defence Force (APM) ambulance to Besut Hospital for further treatment,” he told reporters here today.
Bernama reported earlier today that the father and son had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Islamic affairs gets RM3.1b, as minister outlines support for ‘pondok’ schools, imams and halal SMEs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — The Madani Government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under Budget 2027 to strengthen Islamic development, including support for religious education institutions and the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government’s commitment to a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.
“The Madani Government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for
sekolah agama rakyat
(community religious schools),
tahfiz
institutions and
sekolah pondok
(traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
“The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions,” he said in a statement here today.
Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including
Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain
(Kafa) teachers,
takmir
teachers, imams, bilals,
tok siaks
,
nojas
and
marbuts
, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 Kafa teachers who taught students with special needs, including those who used sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.
“The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation contributions for 40,000 imams, bilals,
tok siaks
, mosque staff and
takmir
teachers.
“The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the ummah,” he said.
In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of diyat, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person’s actions.
Zulkifli said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.
In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300
pondok
schools nationwide.
Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government’s approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.
“This Budget 2027 framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground.
“We aim to elevate the nation’s economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision,” he said.
He added that the government’s priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Jakim is the abbreviation for Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia in Malay, or the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia in English.
Tahfiz
refers to the memorisation of the Quran and, in this context, institutions dedicated to teaching it.
Takmir
refers to religious classes or activities organised to enliven and strengthen mosque life.
Kafa
stands for Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain, or Quran and Fardu Ain classes that teach children Quran recitation and memorisation, as well as basic Islamic religious obligations and practices.
Bilal
refers to a mosque official who assists the imam and calls Muslims to prayer.
Tok siak
refers to a mosque caretaker or attendant.
Noja
(plural: nojas) refers to a person responsible for maintaining a mosque and assisting with its daily operations.
Marbut
refers to a mosque caretaker or person responsible for its upkeep.

Title: Selangor Islamic council denies Jais ‘frame-up’ claims in Nik Nazmi’s khalwat detention, says no one is above the law
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) has denied allegations that the detention of former Setiawangsa MP Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) last Thursday over a khalwat case was an act of persecution or a “frame-up”.
Mais chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said Jais had acted on an official complaint and followed established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual.
“The suggestion that the religious department was involved in manipulation or anything of the sort is entirely untrue.
“We have a legal obligation... when a complaint is lodged, we are required to conduct a thorough investigation.
“Rest assured, Jais will carry out the investigation as diligently as possible, and if there is clear evidence, we will proceed with charges in court,” he said.
He told reporters this after the 2026 Gathering of Accredited Religious Teachers in Selangor at the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Silver Jubilee Hall here today, which was also attended by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.
Salehuddin said the case was made public to clarify that Syariah laws were enforced fairly, regardless of the background or influence of the individual under investigation.
He urged the public to give Jais sufficient time and space to complete its investigation and refrain from speculation that could compromise the fairness of the legal process.
“We cannot pass judgment while the investigation is still incomplete.
“We must act fairly and carry out our duties in accordance with the regulations.
“If we were to act outside these regulations, we ourselves would be subject to accusations,” he said.
Earlier, Nik Nazmi confirmed in a statement on his Instagram account that he was one of two individuals detained by Jais in Petaling Jaya last Thursday over allegations of khalwat, and said he was prepared to cooperate with any legal proceedings.
On a separate case involving a local youth suspected of participating in the rituals of another religion, Salehuddin said preliminary findings suggested that the individual’s actions were, so far, a matter of personal belief.
However, he said Jais was examining various forms of digital evidence, including social media posts concerning rituals at Batu Caves that had been linked to other belief systems.
“The public must understand that when we intend to take legal action in court, we must ensure that all evidence is authentic.
“We are aware that material could potentially be superimposed or generated via AI (artificial intelligence); therefore, we have experts who can verify its authenticity.
“Regarding the issue of apostasy, we cannot impose penalties without conducting a thorough investigation.
“We certainly consult with the relevant authorities before taking action against anyone.
“A comprehensive investigation must be carried out first,” he said.
On October 13, Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said a man who went viral over allegations that he had performed rituals of another religion in breach of Syariah law had been detained alongside his mother in Kuala Lumpur to assist in an investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The acronym Mais in Malay stands for Majlis Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Council. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department.

Title: Stop dumping pet fish in lakes, govt warns as alien species wiping out natives in Ampang lake
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Alien fish account for 95 per cent of fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir, posing a serious threat to the balance of Malaysia’s freshwater ecosystem.
Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak said mitigation efforts needed to be strengthened through data-driven approaches, community education and strategic cooperation involving the government, private sector and non-governmental organisations.
He warned that releasing pet fish into lakes, dams and public waterways when they grow too large or become difficult to care for could harm aquatic biodiversity and threaten the survival of local species.
“If we do not educate, this matter will become a culture that is difficult to curb and will become a long-term problem,” he said at the “Program Kelestarian Perikanan Darat: Mitigasi Memburu Ikan Asing” at Tasik Ampang Hilir here today.
The alien fish-catching programme, conducted from 2022 to 2025, recorded a total catch of 19.74 tonnes, highlighting the need to address the spread of these species more seriously.
Isham said measures included increasing efforts to catch alien fish, releasing local fish fry to help restore the balance of fish populations and expanding public education to discourage people from releasing pet fish into public waters.
He said the ministry was also reviewing ways to tighten existing regulations, including the possibility of banning certain fish species identified as threats to local ecosystems.
Agrobank released 1,400 native fish fry into the lake to support the conservation of local species, comprising 1,100 baung and 300 lampam sungai.
Records from the Malaysian Department of Fisheries showed that 146 of the 154 fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir were alien species, while only eight were native species.
Agrobank chief development officer Ahmad Arif Abu Bakar said efforts to restore the balance between native and alien fish populations needed to be supported by greater public awareness and education on the importance of protecting Malaysia’s biodiversity.
“The public needs to understand their responsibility in maintaining the ecosystem, including not releasing pet fish into rivers or lakes when the fish grow larger,” he said.
The programme brought together about 250 participants from seven agencies and organisations, with activities including catching alien fish using seine nets, cast nets, fishing lines and fish traps. — Bernama

Title: Penang’s RM420m link road to Silicon Island targets first bridge opening by 2028
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — A total of 202.3 hectares of land have been reclaimed at Silicon Island since reclamation works began in September 2023, marking progress in the development of Penang’s next economic growth hub as of October 2026.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the development was envisioned to complement the state’s semiconductor industry while attracting investments in advanced technology, research and development, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovation.
“The early launch of the Silicon Island Experience Centre offers visitors a closer look at our vision for a new growth hub that will complement Penang’s semiconductor industry and attract investments in advanced technology, research and development, and AI-driven innovation,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said Silicon Island was also expected to create quality jobs, develop local talent and benefit surrounding communities, with sustainability remaining a key priority.
Chow said the state government hoped that, with the right support and strategic partnerships, it could take Penang’s economy to the next level and build a stronger, greener future for generations to come.
In a separate statement, Silicon Island Development Sdn Bhd said the Silicon Island Experience Centre was now open to government agencies, investors, local communities and strategic partners to help them better understand the 931-hectare development.
It said the 2,500-square-foot facility featured an interactive LED scale model showcasing key components of the development, including a 283-hectare Green Tech Park, commercial precincts, transit corridors and more than 110 kilometres of dedicated cycling and pedestrian paths.
Built at a cost of RM2.5 million, the centre was completed in four months.
Silicon Island is designed as a smart city with a five-diamond Low Carbon City accreditation, with its development expected to support Penang’s long-term economic growth while incorporating sustainable urban planning.
Penang Infrastructure Corporation Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and Silicon Island Development chairman Datuk Seri Farizan Darus said reclamation works began in September 2023, with 202.3 hectares of land physically reclaimed as of October 2026.
“Physical progress on the RM420 million Pan Island Link 2A contract is also moving smoothly.
“We are targeting the opening of the first section of the marine bridge connecting Jalan Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island by December 2028, leading towards full completion by June 2029,” he said. — Bernama

Title: From USJ to Shah Alam, flash floods disrupt Klang Valley roads after afternoon downpour
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Afternoon thunderstorms brought flash floods to several parts of the Klang Valley today, inundating roads and disrupting traffic in Selangor as authorities urged motorists to avoid affected areas.
Social media posts reported flooding in USJ 1, USJ 7, Sunway, Ara Damansara, Kota Damansara, Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Baru Hicom and Shah Alam, with motorists warned to plan their journeys carefully.
In Shah Alam, the city council warned of rising water levels near the traffic lights at i-City in Section 7 and Padang Jawa in Section 16, advising the public to drive cautiously and avoid affected roads if water levels continued to rise.
The Malaysian Highway Authority also reported flash floods at Ramp C of the Guthrie Corridor Expressway interchange from Shah Alam towards Bukit Jelutong at 5.40pm, with the left lane blocked and only the right lane passable, although traffic was reported to be under control.
The flooding followed an earlier warning from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of the country, including Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat in Selangor.
The weather warning also covered areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Terengganu, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan, Johor and Sarawak, with the forecast conditions expected until 3pm.
On social media, a user warned motorists in USJ to plan their routes, saying: “For those in USJ, plan your route — flooding and traffic jams.”
Another Facebooker reported falling into a drain during flooding in Sunway, writing: “Sunway was flooded earlier, then I fell into a drain and got soaked.”
The Shah Alam City Council advised the public to monitor updates through its i-LenSA portal at ilensa.mbsa.gov.my or contact its 24-hour Pantas hotline at 03-5510 5811.
Motorists were urged to remain alert, avoid driving through floodwaters and check road conditions before setting out.

Title: GRS takes its election pitch to Kudat, with Hajiji eyeing 16 parliamentary seats
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor is scheduled to address more than 3,000 delegates and observers at the 2026 GRS Convention in Kudat tomorrow (Sunday), which aims to prepare the coalition to win at least 16 of the 26 parliamentary seats.
“Although GRS was returned to power in the State election in November last year, the convention also serves to remind that GRS should not rest on its laurels but continue to work hard towards the betterment of the State and people.
“Cooperation and unity among GRS components as well as our partners in the State Unity Government is vital to ensure a decisive victory for GRS in the coming general election,” said Hajiji, who is GRS Chairman and PGRS President.
The inaugural convention in Kudat will be held at Dewan Tun Mustapha, with participants and observers representing all 26 parliamentary constituencies in Sabah, including Labuan.Hajiji said the venue follows a decision by the GRS Supreme Council that the convention should be rotated among the various districts instead of being centred solely in Kota Kinabalu.
Besides Hajiji’s keynote address, the six GRS Deputy Chairmen will deliver speeches. They represent the core leadership of the six GRS component parties, namely PGRS, PBS, PCS, LDP, PHRS and Upko.
Hajiji said the convention will bring together central leadership and key divisional leaders for discussions and sharing sessions with two focuses.
The first is political strategy to strengthen party preparedness, particularly ahead of the 16th General Election.
The second is an assessment of progress on the development agenda for the people and the State under the GRS Manifesto, specifically by advancing the Hala Tuju Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) 2.0 roadmap.
He said GRS’ partners in the State Government are also expected to perform well and deliver more seats so that Sabah’s voice can be heard in Parliament.
Hajiji added that the political dynamics in Sabah favour GRS and the coalition will enter the general election with full confidence of gaining the trust of voters.
The choice of Kudat is seen by many as a sign of GRS’ confidence in capturing the Kota Marudu and Kudat parliamentary seats, which are held by Parti KDM and an Independent respectively. Both Members of Parliament lost in the State election in November last year to GRS candidates.­ — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: GRS stands for Gabungan Rakyat Sabah; PGRS stands for Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah; PBS stands for Parti Bersatu Sabah; PCS stands for Parti Cinta Sabah; LDP stands for Liberal Democratic Party; PHRS stands for Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah; Upko stands for United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation; and SMJ stands for Sabah Maju Jaya.

Title: Sarawak polls could be as early as November, says state minister Abdul Karim
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — Sarawak could hold its 13th state election as early as November, with the polling window extending to mid-December, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
“The window is getting smaller. I would say we only have about one and a half months — November and half of December,” he told reporters at an event here.
Abdul Karim, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief, said the timing would depend on when Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg dissolves the Sarawak Legislative Assembly.
The Election Commission (EC) would then determine the polling date in accordance with the law, he said.
He added that the election timetable must allow sufficient time for the EC to prepare and for campaigning to take place.
A state election must be held within 60 days of the Assembly’s dissolution, a deadline that also applies if its term expires automatically. — Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: The abbreviation DUN in Malay stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri, or State Legislative Assembly.

Title: Melaka polls: PKR to field experienced, young and women candidates, says Amirudin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to firm up its direction for the Melaka state election within a week, with candidate selection now in its final stages, coalition election strategy director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today.
He said the coalition wanted to field candidates with a record of serving the community and relevant experience, while giving newcomers opportunities in some constituencies where its traditional support was weaker.
