“In some state constituencies where our support is relatively low, we will allow candidates to gain experience. This is part of the party’s and Pakatan Harapan’s long-term plan,” he told reporters after attending the Semarak Kasih event with Yayasan Selangor students here, national news wire
Bernama
reported.
Amirudin said allowing candidates to gain experience in less favourable constituencies could help build a longer-term plan for PKR and the wider coalition.
He also touched on possible cooperation with Bersatu, saying the matter had not been finalised and a decision would be made soon.
PKR has previously confirmed that it will contest nine seats in the Melaka election.
Party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said Pakatan Harapan would contest more seats overall if PKR’s allocation remained at nine.
PH is scheduled to announce its candidate on October 24.
The Melaka state election has been set for November 14 with nominations on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two.

Title: Home minister: 24-hour border watch, jetty demolitions to curb cross-border crime in Kelantan
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — Police are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance along all border routes in Kelantan to curb cross-border crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the directive had been issued to Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat to ensure continuous physical surveillance along the border.
“Among the measures taken are the demolition of illegal jetties and enforcement of the law against individuals crossing the border without valid documents,” he told a press conference after attending the launch ceremony for the 2026 Home Ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives here today.
However, he said enforcement measures might not completely eliminate cross-border crime, as it involves organised criminal networks that had been operating for a long time.
Therefore, Saifuddin Nasution said efforts to curb such activities required the cooperation of all parties and could not rely solely on the Home Ministry and the police.
Meanwhile, when asked to comment on the case involving an incident concerning Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, he said police were completing several aspects of the investigation papers after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) requested improvements before a further decision could be made.
Saifuddin Nasution said the investigation papers had been submitted to the AGC within a week of the incident.
He said the AGC subsequently asked police to complete several aspects of the investigation to ensure that the information and evidence gathered were sufficient for further consideration.
He said the investigation papers included witness statements and information gathered throughout the investigation.
The AGC could return the investigation papers to police for further completion if additional information was required before a decision was made, he added.
Previously, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was reported as saying that the investigation was being conducted by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which deals with voluntarily causing hurt to another person.
Mohd Khalid said statements had been recorded from 25 witnesses so far to assist in the investigation into the incident, which occurred on September 28.
The media had earlier reported that Mohd Shuhaily had left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following a viral video showing him reprimanding an individual at KLIA Terminal 1.
Mohd Shuhaily said the matter had been brought to the attention of the country’s top leadership and the Home Ministry, and that he was prepared to accept any decision on the issue. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry: Over 6,700 officers approved for promotions and acting appointments, including four chopper crash victims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — A total of 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the Ministry of Health (MOH) have been approved for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15.
The approvals were granted by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on October 13, according to a statement issued today.
The move reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to recognise officers’ commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.
In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under MOH’s teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.
The approval provides the officers concerned with better opportunities for career advancement.
The ministry also paid tribute to four officers who served with the Flying Doctor Service (PDU) and died in a helicopter crash while on duty on September 8.
All four were approved for posthumous promotions in recognition of their service and dedication.
The ministry expressed confidence that such recognition would encourage continued excellence and strengthen officers’ commitment to building a high-quality, sustainable and responsive national healthcare system.
It will continue to review and implement improvements to ensure officers’ welfare and career development receive due attention. — Bernama

Title: ‘That is not our job’: Amirudin rejects claims PKR plotted khalwat trap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari today denied allegations that the party orchestrated a khalwat case involving former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad to undermine a political rival.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PKR had never discussed or arranged any plan, privately or publicly, to entrap political opponents, news outlet Harian Metro reported.
“We have many other things to do than arrange khalwat cases.
“That is not our job,” he told reporters after launching the Semarak Kasih Yayasan Selangor 2026 programme today.
He added that the party did not want personal matters to become the basis of political rivalry or debate.
Khalwat is an offence under Islamic law involving a Muslim man and woman who are not married to each other being found alone together in circumstances that may suggest improper conduct.
The allegations surfaced after the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained two people in Petaling Jaya last Thursday to assist investigations into a suspected khalwat offence.
The department confirmed yesterday that a man and a woman had been detained at about 6pm in Petaling Jaya under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, but did name the people involved.
Nik Nazmi, a PKR member for almost 21 years till his exit in May, confirmed publicly earlier today that he was one of two people detained and apologised to his wife, family and his current party over what he described as a lapse in judgement.
Parti Bersama Malaysia has since announced that its 44-year-old co-founder is to be suspended three months from October 20 following the khalwat scandal.

Title: KL Immigration to probe alleged irregularities in special pass issuance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office.
Its director, Datuk Hamsha Injau, said the department’s Integrity Division would conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the allegations and that no misconduct would be tolerated.
“Appropriate action will be taken if there is evidence of any breach of the law or regulations,” he said in a statement today.
He also advised the public to deal with the Immigration Department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.
A news portal reported today that special passes, which are intended to assist foreign nationals facing emergencies or urgent circumstances, were allegedly being systematically abused to extend their stay in Malaysia.
The report also alleged that the operation involved local intermediaries who handled applications, collected applicants’ passports and sent their photographs to immigration officers through messaging applications for preliminary verification. — Bernama

Title: N. Sembilan police: Post-mortem finds border agency officer died from pressure on neck, stab wounds
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 17 — Police said preliminary post-mortem findings showed that pressure applied to the neck caused the death of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found at a government staff quarters in Nilai.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the finding followed a nearly five-hour post-mortem examination that began at 9.40 am today at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here.
“The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two on the abdomen and one on the right cheek,” he said in a statement.
On October 15, the woman, who was in her 30s, was found dead at the quarters after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband, reportedly following a misunderstanding.
Alzafny had earlier said police received a report about the incident at 9.30pm after the victim’s husband, also in his 30s, turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported her death.
He was subsequently remanded until October 22 to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Army to review SOP after serviceman arrested with pistol, ammunition and ketum, says chief
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur.
Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army’s continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified.
“The same applies to this case. We are constantly monitoring. Although an SOP is already in place, we are always looking at continuous improvement,” he told reporters after the Passing Out Parade of Young Male Soldiers Series 206/26, involving 1,485 soldiers, here today.
The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Azhan said the individual, who is in his 30s, was undergoing a six-month transition training programme and was scheduled to complete his service in three months.
“For your information, the individual is undergoing transition training before completing his service and is currently detained at Sungai Buloh Prison for the trial process and further action,” he said.
He added that TDM would extend full cooperation to the authorities, including by providing the necessary information on the case.
Meanwhile, Malek Razak said the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) had its own procedures and investigation protocols for handling cases involving its personnel to ensure that all actions were taken in accordance with established regulations. — Bernama

Title: MAF reviewing allowances to boost reserve force participation, says Chief of Defence Force
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force.
Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces.
He said the current hourly rates of RM9.80 and RM8 were relatively low, having last been reviewed around 2022.
“We want them to participate actively in training and activities organised by their respective regiments. Active involvement also gives them additional points if they wish to join the regular force, making the screening process easier,” he told reporters after the passing-out parade for 1,485 recruits from the 206/26 Series of Male Young Soldiers Training here today. Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman was also present.
Malek Razak said an estimated 40 to 50 per cent of registered reserve personnel were inactive, including failing to attend training when called up.
Under existing policy, those who remain inactive for several months or years are removed from the membership list, he said, adding that this hindered efforts to maintain the Territorial Army as a reserve force.
“Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel,” he said.
To improve participation, the MAF will diversify training methods, upgrade infrastructure and strengthen promotional efforts.
Malek Razak said graduates of the Reserve Officers Training Unit (PALAPES) were given priority to join the regular armed forces through the graduate officer recruitment scheme and could also receive additional academic credits.
“We believe it is a waste for them to undergo military training, particularly as officers, only to leave after completing their studies. We want them to become the next generation of officers in the regular service,” he said.
In a separate development, he said the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) would hand over some support assets to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) following the planned termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) mission early next year.
The assets include generators, general-purpose vehicles and other equipment that would not need to be returned to Malaysia.
Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said 292 assets worth an estimated US$10 million (about RM42 million) would be handed over in stages until January 2027 for welfare, humanitarian assistance and peacekeeping efforts for local communities.
Malek Razak also urged young people to join the MAF, particularly in technology, artificial intelligence (AI) and information technology (IT), to support the modernisation of the armed forces. — Bernama

Title: Home minister: Immigration depots facing capacity pressure amid daily enforcement operations
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — Immigration depots nationwide are facing capacity pressures due to daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the continuous arrival of individuals detained during enforcement operations had led to overcrowding.
The increase in detainees is also result of the Immigration Department’s mapping of areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.
“The mapping exercise enables the authorities to identify areas that are frequently used as settlements or gathering places by foreign nationals.
“Those detained may include individuals without travel documents, those holding expired passes, those who have misused their passes, or individuals with refugee status,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution was speaking at a press conference after attending the Home Ministry’s 2026 Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School launch ceremony here today.
He said action against each category had to take into account the individuals’ respective status and legal position, adding that enforcement operations also involved other enforcement agencies and local authorities.
Meanwhile, Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu had been identified as the four states recording drug-related case rates above the national threshold, based on figures per 100,000 population.
Saifuddin Nasution explained that the assessment was based on data from four sources, using a calculation method that referred to international standards.
Pendang in Kedah recorded the highest rate in the country, followed by Kuala Krai in second place.
Other districts identified were Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, all of which recorded rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.
The data would be used to identify areas requiring more targeted prevention and enforcement measures, he said.
Saifuddin Nasution stressed that cooperation between the Home Ministry, National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK), police and state governments was crucial to intensifying awareness and prevention programmes in the affected areas.
These efforts would include community outreach programmes to educate the public and raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said about 75 per cent of the 90,000 inmates in prisons nationwide were involved in drug-related offences.
He said most of the inmates had been involved in offences under Sections 15(1) (self-administration), 12 (restriction on import and export of certain dangerous drugs) and 39 (general penalty) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“Of the 41 prisons nationwide, Pengkalan Chepa Prison in Kota Bharu is among the most overcrowded.
“Based on the profile of prison inmates, those aged between 15 and 39 make up the largest group, while the involvement of children under 15 in drug-related cases is also a cause for concern,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution said the data also showed that unemployed people made up the largest group of those involved in drug abuse.
Commenting on patterns of drug abuse, he said synthetic drugs were more commonly linked to cases on the east coast, while drug use on the west coast involved a combination of synthetic and non-synthetic substances, adding that the use of synthetic drugs was particularly high because they were more readily available. — Bernama

Title: Bersama suspends Nik Nazmi from party activities for three months from Oct 20 after Jais incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Parti Bersama Malaysia has suspended Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months, effective October 20.
The party said the decision followed his public admission regarding his involvement in an incident with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) in Petaling Jaya on October 15.
In his earlier statement, Nik Nazmi
confirmed
he was the man caught with a woman, who is not his
muhrim
(a legally permissible close relative), in an enclosed space during the raid, and publicly apologised to his wife, family and party members.
“Bersama views this development seriously and takes the position that every issue involving the party’s leadership and members must be addressed appropriately to preserve the party’s integrity, credibility and public confidence,” Syukri Razab said in a statement on behalf of the party.
The suspension will run until January 19, 2027.
The party stated that the decision was necessary and reasonable, without denying Nik Nazmi’s contributions and commitment to Bersama since the party was relaunched in May 2026.

Title: Drug abuse among Malaysian under-15s a growing concern, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group.
He added that this development necessitates a preventive approach that also emphasises early education and the role of parents in curbing the involvement of youngsters in drug abuse.
“The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has three main functions, namely education and prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation, to address the issue of drug abuse.
“Efforts to educate the public must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage preventive action among families,” he told a media conference after attending the Home Ministry’s Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School 2026 launching ceremony here today.
Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.
He said the aircraft had departed from Subang for Laos without any drugs on board, before the consignment was loaded into the plane when it was in that country.
“Laotian authorities detected the drugs when the aircraft was about to continue its flight to Manila,.
“Police have traced the aircraft’s owner, as well as its pilot and co-pilot, to assist in the investigation as the aircraft had departed from Subang,” he said.
He said investigation was also focusing on the party that charted the aircraft, the purpose of the charter and its intended destination.
Saifuddin Nasution said the aircraft owner’s identity had been established, but further details of the investigation could not yet be disclosed.
Previously, Lao police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 individuals arrested in connection with the case.
The Vientiane Times, quoting the Lao Security Newspaper, reported that the security operation was conducted on October 1 following information received by provincial police on Sept 21 regarding a drug trafficking syndicate believed to be planning to smuggle narcotics across the border by air, using a private aircraft.
According to the report, police subsequently received information about a change in the flight schedule, with the private jet expected to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30 pm on October 1. — Bernama

Title: Lawyer: Zara Qairina’s mother yet to decide on civil action as inquest nears conclusion
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest.
Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action.
“For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions. We will discuss the matter with our client, as the final decision on whether to take civil action against any party deemed responsible rests with her,” he told a press conference after the inquest proceedings yesterday.
Shahlan also revealed that Noraidah had sent a brief WhatsApp message that morning, expressing her hope that everything would be made easier.
He thanked members of the media for their coverage of the inquest, describing it as professional, accurate and timely.
Shahlan said the 96-day inquest had been a challenging process, although it had proceeded relatively swiftly alongside proceedings in the Court for Children.
“There is a lot that we need to address in our written submissions, and we hope the decision eventually reached will be fair to all parties,” he said.
On the funds raised to support the inquest, Shahlan clarified that the amount collected was slightly more than RM200,000, dismissing claims that it had reached RM1 million or RM2 million.
He said the fund was announced by Senator Marhamah Rosli last year and had been independently audited after Noraidah and the legal team appointed a qualified independent accountant in April this year.
According to Shahlan, the money was intended solely to cover expenses related to the inquest and had not been used for other purposes.
He added that the legal team had handled the case on a pro bono basis, meaning no legal fees were charged.
Shahlan also said there was no legal requirement for Noraidah or the legal team to make the audit report publicly available. — Daily Express

Title: Man loses RM363,887 in alleged fake bank auction property scam in Miri
Article:
MIRI, Oct 17 — A man who intended to buy a property for his family has allegedly been cheated out of RM363,887.49 in a non-existent bank auction property deal.
Miri District Police Chief ACP Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said in a statement shared on Miri police’s official social media page that the 56-year-old victim lodged a police report at Miri Central Police Station on October 15.
According to the police report, the victim had known the suspect for about two years through business dealings and friendship.
“In November 2025, the complainant intended to purchase a house for family use in Kuching. The suspect then allegedly offered five houses in the Taman Abadi area, Kuching, which were claimed to be bank auction houses at prices lower than the market rate.
“The suspect also offered to manage the purchase process, including the preparation of the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and property title transfer,” said the statement.
Mohd Farhan said the complainant claimed to have made several payments in stages between November 2025 and January 2026 for the proposed purchases, including deposits, land surveying fees and payments related to the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
“However, the purchase arrangements were allegedly not completed as promised. The complainant also claimed that they have yet to receive complete documents proving ownership of the houses, despite contacting the suspect repeatedly for clarification,” he said.
Police are investigating the case under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and dishonestly inducing the delivery of property.
Police advised the public to be cautious of property offers at unrealistically low prices, verify property status through official channels, consult qualified lawyers and avoid transferring money to third-party accounts without proper verification. — The Borneo Post

Title: Transport minister: RM1,000 aid for remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers to be paid via EFT
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — The remaining eligible taxi, rental car and school bus drivers nationwide will receive the RM1,000 Special Financial Aid directly into their respective bank accounts through Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the disbursement through this method would be carried out in the next phase, following the first phase of direct handovers to eligible drivers in several zones.
He said that in the first phase, the aid would be handed directly to eligible recipients in selected zones, with Penang hosting the second presentation ceremony after the launch in Putrajaya on October 14.
“For the second ceremony, we are very pleased to be able to bring together 700 taxi and rental car drivers in Penang, who were selected as symbolic representatives to receive the aid in person.
“All the aid will be handed over to those who have been verified as eligible before Deepavali,” he told reporters after the special financial aid presentation ceremony for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers at Dewan Sri Pinang here today.
He also reminded drivers to ensure that they met the eligibility requirements to facilitate the screening of recipient data.
The main requirements include holding a driver card and a valid vehicle licence or permit (VP), as well as a valid Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licence.
Loke also urged drivers to keep abreast of announcements by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD), the Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) Sabah and LPKP Sarawak regarding the required information and verification process.
He said coordination among agencies under the Transport Ministry was important to ensure that the screening of recipient data was carried out transparently and fairly.
“I know that this RM1,000 may not solve all your problems or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs. However, I sincerely hope this assistance can, to some extent, ease your household expenses, help you replace worn-out tyres or fill your fuel tanks so that you can continue going out to earn a living,” he said.
On October 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a one-off RM1,000 special financial aid for taxi, rental car and school bus drivers as one of the initiatives under Budget 2027. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia records 5,278 domestic violence cases, with numbers still climbing, says Nancy Shukri (VIDEO)
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — A total of 5,278 domestic violence cases have been reported in Malaysia, with the number continuing to rise, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said the ministry was placing greater emphasis on counselling and women’s empowerment to help women better understand their rights, build confidence and achieve financial independence.
“When women are financially independent, they can be more confident in standing up for themselves and are less likely to tolerate abuse,” Nancy told reporters at the EmpowerUS 2026 seminar at the Sarawak State Library here today.
https://www.facebook.com/borneopost.online/videos/a-total-of-5278-domestic-violence-cases-have-been-reported-in-malaysia-with-the-/1385867886638367/
Commenting on the recent case in Negeri Sembilan involving a 35-year-old female customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband, Nancy said the ministry was looking into providing assistance to the victim’s family and children.
“We are making preparations to provide assistance, particularly for the children and the family of the victim,” she said, adding that the ministry remained ready to assist families in need.
In July and August, 632 domestic violence cases were recorded in each month, up from 601 in June.
However, the figures remained below the 766 cases recorded in April, the highest monthly total so far in 2026.
Meanwhile, Talian Kasih recorded 104,784 calls as of October 2026, surpassing the 98,050 calls received throughout 2025.
Nancy said the increase in calls indicated growing public awareness of the helpline and the assistance it provides.
“Even children know what to do. It is not just for abuse; it is also for those who are facing problems with their families and need help,” she added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawakian couple allegedly paid three friends RM8,000 each to smuggle cocaine into Japan, says Bukit Aman
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — A Sarawakian husband and wife allegedly recruited three friends to traffic cocaine into Japan, said Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan.
The Star reported that each of the three friends was paid RM8,000 and was believed to have known they were carrying contraband.
“We believe they knew what they were carrying. At the very least, they knew they were carrying something illegal,” he said at a press conference at Johor police headquarters on Friday.
Hussein said the couple had invited their three friends on what was presented as a holiday in Japan.
Each was given a pair of shoes containing concealed drugs before travelling to Kuala Lumpur International Airport for their flight to Tokyo.
The five suspects, all Sarawakians, were arrested at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo last Saturday after Japanese authorities discovered 5kg of cocaine concealed in the insoles of their shoes.
Police have also identified a sixth suspect who managed to return to Malaysia.
None of the five suspects had prior criminal records, and investigations are ongoing to determine whether they had travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi. — The Borneo Post

Title: Slain border agency officer’s remains to be buried in Tumpat tonight, says home minister
Article:
MACHANG, Oct 17 — The remains of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency officer allegedly killed by her husband in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, underwent a post-mortem this morning before being transported to Tumpat, Kelantan, for burial.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the remains were being transported by road and were expected to arrive in Tumpat tonight.
He said the suspect had recently been released from prison after serving a sentence for a drug-related offence.
“The victim leaves behind two children, aged five and six, who are now being cared for by her older sister,” he told a press conference after attending the launch of the Home Ministry’s 2026 Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives here today.
The officer was found dead last Thursday at the staff quarters of Kuala Lumpur International Airport, in an incident in which she was believed to have been killed by her husband.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad reportedly said police received information about the incident at 8.30pm that day.
Meanwhile, Kampung Gosong here has received RM500,000 to upgrade public facilities and residents’ homes under the ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani initiative.
Saifuddin said the upgrades would cover the mosque, surau, toilets, ablution areas and cemetery, alongside repairs to 14 houses.
He said the house repairs were being carried out in collaboration with Akademi Binaan Malaysia and involved 10 individuals under the supervision of the Prisons Department, as well as members of the People’s Volunteer Corps.
In a related development, Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambul Lawar received RM100,000 under the Sekolah Angkat Madani initiative to upgrade its facilities, including the ceiling, toilets, water supply, computer laboratory and guard post.
The school had also been equipped with smart boards to improve pupils’ interaction during teaching and learning sessions.
In addition, 82 villagers and 54 students received zakat assistance distributed through the corporate zakat wakalah scheme of PBLT Sdn Bhd. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: AKPS stands for Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan Malaysia, or Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency. KLIA stands for Kuala Lumpur International Airport. ABM stands for Akademi Binaan Malaysia, or Malaysian Construction Academy. Rela stands for Ikatan Relawan Rakyat Malaysia, or Malaysia Volunteer Corps.

Title: Ports, railways and highways could be next in Malaysia’s 5G coverage push
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Oct 17 — The Communications Ministry and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will study expanding telecommunications coverage targets, particularly for 5G, to include key economic areas such as ports, rail lines and highways.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the current Coverage of Populated Area (CoPA) metric should be reviewed to account for connectivity needs in areas with few or no residents but significant economic activity.
“CoPA is frequently used by telecommunications companies and international bodies to refer to connectivity in populated areas. However, when we talk about 5G access, areas such as ports have no residents but are hubs for significant economic activities,” he said.
He said Malaysia would also raise the issue at international forums, including an International Telecommunication Union (ITU) meeting in Doha in November, to discuss extending 5G and future technologies beyond populated areas to economic hubs.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after launching the Penang Port Private 5G initiative at the North Butterworth Container Terminal (NBCT) today, making Penang Port the first port in Malaysia to adopt a private 5G network through a collaboration between Altel Communications Sdn Bhd (Altel) and Penang Port.
Also present were Penang Deputy Chief Minister II Jagdeep Singh Deo, Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general for telecommunications infrastructure V. Mano and MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali.
Fahmi said reliable connectivity was essential for industrial operations and that telecommunications infrastructure should not be concentrated solely in populated areas.
Private 5G networks could also be expanded to manufacturing and logistics, particularly for multinational companies (MNCs) operating in Malaysia, he added.
He said the technology offered dedicated connectivity and could support more devices simultaneously, including machinery and equipment requiring high precision.
Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesman, said his ministry would prepare a Cabinet memorandum on the proposal and work with the Ministry of Transport (MOT) to extend coverage, including through 5G deployment at other ports.
He cited previous cooperation between the two ministries to address internet connectivity gaps along major rail routes, including sections managed by Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB).
“Based on our previous cooperation with MOT, I believe we can expand these efforts, including by leveraging 5G technology, regardless of who provides the service, for deployment at ports,” he said.
Fahmi said private 5G networks differed from conventional networks by providing dedicated communication channels for critical industrial operations, without requiring users to share network capacity with others.
He said the technology should also be adopted more widely by private-sector operators, including manufacturers and oil palm plantation companies, to improve operational efficiency and safety. — Bernama

Title: Motorists say RON95 wrecked their engines, and Selangor is now investigating seven petrol stations over watery fuel claims
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 17 — Selangor is investigating seven petrol stations after motorists complained that RON95 petrol suspected of being contaminated with water had damaged their vehicle engines, following similar allegations in northern states earlier this month.
Selangor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry director Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari said the ministry had received 10 official complaints involving the seven premises and collected 27 petrol samples for laboratory analysis.
“Investigations found that consumer complaints involved various symptoms of engine damage, such as abnormal engine noises, jerking, loss of power, engines failing to start and cases of burnt engine valves,” he was quoted by news outlet
Harian Metro
as saying today.
Hanif said some vehicle service centres had confirmed that water contamination in fuel tanks was responsible for engine damage in complainants’ vehicles.
Initial inspections found that all seven stations had valid Special Approval Licences and licences under the Petroleum Development Act 1974.
However, the ministry issued notices requiring the operators to provide relevant documents and information to assist the investigation.
The ministry is investigating possible offences under Section 5(1)(c), read together with Sections 6(1)(d) and 7 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, concerning alleged false trade descriptions relating to the content of the petrol supplied.
Hanif urged oil companies and petrol station operators to maintain their underground storage tanks regularly and comply with fuel quality and safety standards.
Motorists who suspect they have been affected were advised to keep their petrol receipts and workshop inspection reports as evidence when lodging complaints with the ministry.
Earlier complaints in northern states
Earlier this month, Penang’s Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry office reported receiving 33 complaints involving about 30 petrol stations over alleged water contamination in RON95.
An inspection at a station in Batu Kawan found no evidence of water contamination.
In Kedah, the ministry collected samples from 11 stations after motorists reported vehicle breakdowns following refuelling.
In Perak, inspections at six stations in Ipoh, Taiping and Kuala Kangsar found no initial signs of water in the storage tanks examined.
Authorities said laboratory results were needed to determine whether the allegations were substantiated.
There is no confirmed evidence currently that the complaints in Selangor and the northern states are connected.

Title: Haze-hit areas: Parents to decide on childcare attendance, but kids must stay indoors, says family minister
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 17 — No
taska
(childcare centres) have been ordered to close so far due to the haze, but all outdoor activities must be suspended to reduce children’s exposure to polluted air.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the decision not to order a blanket closure of childcare centres took into account the needs of working parents who rely on the services.
She said parents had the discretion to decide whether to send their children to childcare centres, particularly in areas where schools had been ordered to close following high Air Pollutant Index readings.
“We understand that some parents cannot simply leave their children at home because there is no one to look after them.
“So, perhaps parents can discuss with their employers or the respective childcare centre operators on the steps to be taken. However, the main requirement that must be observed is that children must not be allowed to play outdoors,” she told reporters after officiating the Empowerus 2026, themed ‘Empowering Leaders: Sustainable, Resilient and Ethical Leadership’, here today.
Nancy advised parents to take their children for medical check-ups if they showed symptoms of illness while the haze persisted. — Bernama

Title: From neighbour disputes to legal reform, Malaysia moves to strengthen community mediation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Ministry of National Unity (KPN) is reviewing proposed improvements to the Mediation Act 2012 to establish a clearer legal framework for strengthening community mediation services under the National Unity and Integration Department (JPNIN).
Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Act, which falls under the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), does not specifically cover the operation of JPNIN’s community mediation services.
He said JPNIN’s mediation services, including training and accreditation for community mediators, were currently based on Section 8(d) of the Rukun Tetangga Act 2012.
However, the provision was insufficient to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the services.
“I have therefore asked JPNIN to meet with BHEUU to review the proposed improvements, including amendments to the Mediation Act 2012, to provide a clearer legal basis for these services,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Seri Kota Public Housing Collaborative Social Project on Community Mediation here today.
Also present was Bandar Tun Razak Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, the prime minister’s wife.
Aaron also called on JPNIN and the National Integration Research and Training Institute (IKLIN) to conduct comparative studies of countries with specific legal frameworks for community mediation, including Singapore, India and Sri Lanka.
He cited Singapore’s Community Mediation Centres Act 1997, India’s Mediation Act 2023 and Sri Lanka’s Mediation Boards Act 1988 as examples for comparison.
The study, he said, would help assess how legislation in these countries regulates the powers and functions of mediation bodies, mediator accreditation, mediation procedures and safeguards for parties involved.
Meanwhile, the government will expand its network of Community Mediation Centres by establishing 12 new centres at strategic locations nationwide this year, including in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; Miri, Sarawak; Pontian, Johor; Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu; and Shah Alam, Selangor.
“These centres will serve as community reference points for information, preliminary advice and appropriate channels to resolve community issues and disputes.
“This approach will help identify and address conflicts early, before they escalate into more serious disputes and strain community relations,” he said.
On the Seri Kota Public Housing Community Mediation Centre, Aaron said it was JPNIN’s 11th such centre.
Its location was selected based on several factors, including a population of nearly 6,000, available local facilities, community demand and the need to address neighbourhood issues.
He said the centre’s establishment also followed a resolution proposed at the 2024 K2K Initiative Development Strategic Workshop organised by Think City in collaboration with government agencies and stakeholders. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The abbreviations KPN stand for Kementerian Perpaduan Negara (Ministry of National Unity); JPNIN stands for Jabatan Perpaduan Negara dan Integrasi Nasional (National Unity and Integration Department); BHEUU stands for Bahagian Hal Ehwal Undang-Undang (Legal Affairs Division); and IKLIN stands for Institut Kajian dan Latihan Integrasi Nasional (National Integration Research and Training Institute).
